lead: A 14th-century monastery, tree-lined avenues and houses with gardens, in one of the wealthiest neighbourhoods in the city.
text: The neighbourhood takes its name from the convent of the Poor Clares that Queen Elisenda de Montcada founded in the 14th century, with a two-storey cloister and a single-nave Gothic church; in the chapel of Sant Miquel the paintings by Ferrer Bassa, from 1346, are preserved.

Today it is a quiet, green neighbourhood of detached houses with gardens and high-end buildings, with Avinguda Pearson as its emblem. At 6,079 €/m² and 1,948 €/month, it has the highest prices in Les Corts. Beside the Diagonal there are also the Palau Reial and Gaudí's Pavellons Güell.
housing: Detached houses with gardens and high-end residential buildings, with generous floor areas.
